note: Attacker-controlled bytes are copied into the in-memory configuration buffer that the parser will read.
The fuzzing entry point wraps the copied bytes in a config object and initializes the lexer/parser state over that buffer.
A '$' followed by '{' diverts the lexer into variable parsing, which is the path implicated by the crash state.
The lexer advances past the '${' prefix and then scans forward for the closing brace or default separator.
When the scanner peeks or backs up at the start of the buffer, this decrement can move the cursor before the beginning of the mapped input, creating the out-of-bounds read condition.
The parser keeps invoking the lexer state machine until a token is produced; the invalid cursor movement is exercised during this repeated lexing loop.
The crash state names backup -> lex_string -> lex_next, so the vulnerable sink is the string lexer’s lookahead/backtrack logic on attacker-controlled '${' input.
